sourcePolicy: Only what was read on the page listed is stated as the source's claim. Full texts behind paywalls (Wiley, Springer, SSRN) were not read; their abstracts were read via RePEc/IDEAS or NBER.

studies.citation: Fama & French (2015), five-factor model; Ken French Data Library 'Fama/French 5 Factors (2x3)'
studies.method: Six value-weight 2x3 portfolios on size and B/M, size and operating profitability (OP), size and investment; formed end of June with accounting data for the fiscal year ending in t-1; NYSE breakpoints; all NYSE, AMEX and NASDAQ stocks. RMW = 1/2 (Small Robust + Big Robust) - 1/2 (Small Weak + Big Weak); HML and CMA analogous. Monthly data from July 1963.
studies.originalStructure: long-short, value-weighted, broadly diversified, annual rebalancing

applicability.US: Directly measurable: the library's long-only sorted portfolios are survivorship-free (CRSP) and lagged; used for the academic-path test.
applicability.KR: Not covered by the library; Korea has no comparable survivorship-free public dataset in this repository.

studies.overlapWithOurSignals: value sleeve (B/P), quality sleeve (roe, margins, leverage) approximate HML and RMW; our sleeves are percentile composites, not 2x3 sorts

studies.method: Strategies that buy past winners and sell past losers generate significant positive returns over three- to twelve-month holding periods; not explained by systematic risk or delayed reaction to common factors; part of the first-year abnormal return dissipates in the following two years (abstract).
studies.originalStructure: long-short winner/loser portfolios across many stocks (details beyond the abstract not read)

applicability.US: Momentum is already in production's momentum sleeve; local rank IC -0.0015 (p 0.92). The library's big-winner portfolio is reported here as descriptive only.
applicability.KR: Already tested: momentum and industry momentum in KR ML tournaments; industry momentum is rebalance-phase dependent.

studies.overlapWithOurSignals: momentum sleeve (12-1 and 6-month returns), industry momentum rule, ML price features

studies.citation: Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen (2019), Quality Minus Junk, Review of Accounting Studies 24(1)
studies.method: Quality = characteristics investors should pay more for: profitability, growth and safety. High-quality stocks have higher prices but not by much and earn high risk-adjusted returns; a QMJ factor (long quality, short junk) earns significant risk-adjusted returns in the US and across 24 countries; the price of quality varies over time and a low price predicts high future QMJ returns (abstract).
studies.originalStructure: long-short factor; component measures and breakpoints not read

applicability.US: Our quality sleeve covers profitability and leverage (safety) only partially; growth and payout components are not built.
applicability.KR: Same; KR quality coverage gaps (value/quality missing 54-55% in the attribution audit).

studies.overlapWithOurSignals: quality sleeve; the four-factor attribution audit measured quality 126D rank IC -0.022 pooled

studies.citation: Novy-Marx (2013), The Other Side of Value: The Gross Profitability Premium, JFE 108(1) 1-28 (NBER w15940)
studies.method: Profitability measured by gross profits-to-assets has roughly the same power as book-to-market in predicting the cross-section of average returns; profitable firms earn higher returns despite lower book-to-market and larger size; controlling for profitability raises value strategy performance, especially among the largest, most liquid stocks (abstract).

applicability.US: Gross profits / assets is not derived in our PIT store (no gross profit or total-assets field); ROE and operating margin are the available proxies. The library's OP sorts are the closest public long-only test.
applicability.KR: DART gross profit coverage not built; not measurable.

studies.overlapWithOurSignals: quality sleeve, S2 value-confirmation (cheap AND confirmed by profit/cash flow)

studies.citation: Novy-Marx (2015), Backtesting Strategies Based on Multiple Signals (NBER w21329)
studies.method: Strategies that combine multiple signals suffer severe overfitting bias because each signal is signed to predict positive in-sample returns; combinations of random signals can look highly significant; appropriate critical values can be several times standard levels; combining the best k of n signals is almost as biased as picking the best of n^k (abstract).

applicability.both: Governs our rules: the B1 screen uses one signal, the academic-path test pre-registers one primary portfolio and a Bonferroni threshold, and no composite is fitted.

studies.overlapWithOurSignals: directly relevant to the four-factor composite, ML tournaments (141 models) and the cocktail policies

timeSeriesVsCrossSection: All five are cross-sectional (which stocks beat others), not forecasts of the market index. Market-timing evidence (C1 exposure, US cocktail) is a separate question and is graded separately.
